definition_en: to change and improve something written, or to study again
core_image: 一页写满批注的稿纸，边角已经卷起
scene: 编辑在页边写下新的批注，要求作者修改第三章。The editor wrote fresh comments in the margin and asked the author to revise the third chapter.
sceneCN: 这里 revise 是「修改、修订」（第 1 个义项：改动文字使其更好）；句意：编辑在页边写下新的批注，要求作者修改第三章。

senses.title: Improving a text
senses.definition: to change a piece of writing to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 改动文字使其更好
senses.example: He revised the report three times.
senses.exampleCN: 他把报告修改了三遍。
senses.why: Re- plus visere, to look at, gives the sense of looking again to improve.
senses.whyCN: re- 加 visere（看）表示再看一遍以求改进。

senses.title: Studying for a test
senses.definition: to study lessons again before an exam
senses.definitionCN: 考试前再次学习功课
senses.example: British students revise for exams in May.
senses.exampleCN: 英国学生在五月为考试复习。
senses.why: British English extends looking again to studying again.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语把再看一遍延伸为再学一遍。

senses.title: Changing a plan
senses.definition: to change a plan or opinion after thinking again
senses.definitionCN: 重新考虑后改变计划或看法
senses.example: We revised our travel plans after the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨后我们调整了旅行计划。
senses.why: Any plan can be looked at again and improved.
senses.whyCN: 任何计划都能被重新审视并改进。

intro.en: Revise comes from Latin revisere, to look at again.
intro.cn: revise 源自拉丁语 revisere（再看）。

items.en: Revisere means to look at again.
items.cn: revisere 意为再看。

items.en: It joins re-, again, to visere, to view.
items.cn: 它由 re-（再）与 visere（看）组成。

items.en: French reviser carries the sense of looking over a text.
items.cn: 法语 reviser 带有通读文本的含义。

items.en: Revise first means to look at writing again.
items.cn: revise 最初指再次审视文字。

items.en: British English adds the sense of studying for exams.
items.cn: 英式英语增加了为考试复习的含义。

note.en: Revise changes a text, while review only looks at it again.
note.cn: revise 是改动文字，review 只是再看一遍。

entries.definition: to make small changes to something

normalIntro.en: Revise is to look again and make the text better.
normalIntro.cn: revise 是再看一遍并让文字更好。

normal.en: Revise a draft means improve the writing.
normal.cn: revise a draft 意为改进文字。

normal.en: Revise for an exam means study again.
normal.cn: revise for an exam 意为再次学习。

normal.en: A revised edition has been changed.
normal.cn: a revised edition 是经过修改的版本。

normal.en: Revise a plan means adjust it.
normal.cn: revise a plan 意为调整计划。

normal.en: Compare edit: edit can cut, revise usually improves.
normal.cn: 对比 edit：edit 可以删减，revise 通常是改进。

abstract.en: Picture a page with arrows and new sentences in the margin.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸，页边画着箭头和新句子。

abstract.en: Imagine polishing a rough stone until it shines.
abstract.cn: 想象把粗糙的石头打磨到发亮。

abstract.en: Think of a second draft that is clearer than the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一份比初稿更清楚的二稿。

examples.en: The author revised the last chapter.
examples.cn: 作者修改了最后一章。

examples.en: She is revising for her history exam.
examples.cn: 她正在为历史考试复习。

examples.en: The company revised its budget.
examples.cn: 公司调整了预算。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ vise（看）」——再看一遍并动手改，就是修订、修改。

root: 拉丁语 revisere（再看）＝ re-（再）＋ visere（看）→ 法语 reviser → revise，核心义「再看一遍并加以改进」。

sensesIntro.en: Revise begins with improving a text, extends to British exam study, and finally to adjusting plans.
sensesIntro.cn: revise 从改进文字开始，延伸到英式英语的考试复习，最后指调整计划。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a marked-up manuscript with curled corners.
core.cn: 核心意象：写满批注、边角卷起的稿纸。

branches.en: Improving a text is the core use.
branches.cn: 改进文字是核心用法。

branches.en: British students look at lessons again.
branches.cn: 英国学生再学一遍功课。

branches.en: Plans are also looked at and changed.
branches.cn: 计划也会被重新审视和改动。

branches.en: Both writing and studying involve a second pass.
branches.cn: 写文章与学习都包含第二遍过程。

branches.en: Texts and plans can both be improved.
branches.cn: 文字与计划都能被改进。

intro.en: Revise joins re-, again, to the Latin root vis, to see.
intro.cn: revise 由 re-（再）与拉丁词根 vis（看）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin videre and its form visere give the word its seeing root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 videre 及其变体 visere 提供了「看」的词根。

latinEntries.example: Visere is a frequentative form of videre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: visere 是 videre 的反复形式。

definition_en: the act of changing a text or studying again
core_image: 三稿叠在一起，最上面一版布满红色改线
scene: 交稿前，她把三稿叠在一起，完成最后一轮修订。Before the deadline, she stacked the three drafts and finished the final revision.
sceneCN: 这里 revision 是「修订」（第 1 个义项：修改文字的行为）；句意：交稿前，她把三稿叠在一起，完成最后一轮修订。

senses.title: Changing a text
senses.definition: the act of changing writing to improve it
senses.definitionCN: 改动文字使其更好的行为
senses.example: The essay needs another revision.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章还需要再修订一次。
senses.why: Revision is the noun of revise, the act of looking again and changing.
senses.whyCN: revision 是 revise 的名词，指再看并改动的行为。

senses.title: A changed version
senses.definition: a version that has been changed
senses.definitionCN: 经过修改的版本
senses.example: The revision is much clearer than the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 修订版比初稿清楚得多。
senses.why: The act produces a new version, which also bears the name.
senses.whyCN: 这一行为产生新版本，新版本也叫 revision。

senses.title: Exam study
senses.definition: study done before an exam
senses.definitionCN: 考试前的学习
senses.example: He did two hours of revision each night.
senses.exampleCN: 他每晚复习两个小时。
senses.why: British English uses revision for the study that precedes an exam.
senses.whyCN: 英式英语用 revision 指考试前的复习。

intro.en: Revision comes from Latin revisio, a looking again, from revisere.
intro.cn: revision 源自拉丁语 revisio（再看），来自 revisere。

items.en: Revisere means to look at again.
items.cn: revisere 意为再看。

items.en: Revisio names the act of looking again.
items.cn: revisio 指再看的行为。

items.en: French revision keeps the act in its name.
items.cn: 法语 revision 在名称中保留了这一行为。

items.en: Revision first names the act of changing text.
items.cn: revision 最初指修改文字的行为。

items.en: British English adds exam study to the meaning.
items.cn: 英式英语又加入了考试复习的含义。

note.en: Revision is the noun; revisionism is a very different idea.
note.cn: revision 是名词；revisionism 指完全不同的历史修正主义。

entries.definition: a small change to a text
a published version of a book
the act of making something right

normalIntro.en: Revision is the second look that leaves red marks.
normalIntro.cn: revision 是留下红色批注的第二次审视。

normal.en: A major revision changes much of the text.
normal.cn: a major revision 改动大部分文字。

normal.en: A final revision is the last check.
normal.cn: a final revision 是最后一次检查。

normal.en: Revision notes help students study.
normal.cn: revision notes 帮助学生复习。

normal.en: The revision of a draft improves it.
normal.cn: 草稿的修订让它变得更好。

normal.en: Compare edition: an edition is printed, a revision is the change itself.
normal.cn: 对比 edition：edition 是印刷版本，revision 是改动本身。

abstract.en: Picture three stacks of paper with red lines across the top.
abstract.cn: 想象三叠纸，最上面一叠布满红线。

abstract.en: Imagine a sculptor cutting away stone for a second time.
abstract.cn: 想象雕塑家第二次凿去石料。

abstract.en: Think of a path being redrawn to reach the same place more easily.
abstract.cn: 想象重新画一条更容易到达同一地点的路。

examples.en: The plan is still under revision.
examples.cn: 计划仍在修订中。

examples.en: We made several revisions to the report.
examples.cn: 我们对报告做了几处修订。

examples.en: Her nightly revision paid off in the exam.
examples.cn: 她每晚的复习在考试中见效了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）＋ vision（看）」——再看一遍并动手改，就是修订。

root: 拉丁语 revisio（再看）→ 法语 revision → revision，核心义「再看并改动的行为及其成果」。

sensesIntro.en: Revision names the act of changing a text, then the changed version, and in British English the study before an exam.
sensesIntro.cn: revision 先指修改文字的行为，再指修改后的版本，英式英语中还指考试前的复习。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three stacked drafts covered in red marks.
core.cn: 核心意象：三叠布满红色批注的稿子。

branches.en: The act of changing text is the core.
branches.cn: 修改文字的行为是核心。

branches.en: A changed version also carries the name.
branches.cn: 修改后的版本也叫这个名字。

branches.en: British study before exams uses the word.
branches.cn: 英式英语用它指考前复习。

branches.en: The act and its result share one noun.
branches.cn: 行为与结果共用一个名词。

branches.en: Both changing text and exam study involve looking again.
branches.cn: 改文章与考前复习都包含再看一遍。

intro.en: Revision is revise plus the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: revision 是 revise 加名词后缀 -ion。

latinIntro.en: Latin revisio gives the word its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 revisio 赋予这个词现在的形态。

latinEntries.example: Revisere leads to the noun revisio.

definition_en: to rise up against a ruler or refuse to accept something
core_image: 广场上的人群举起手，旗帜在风里翻卷
scene: 粮价上涨后，城里的居民起来反抗，要求罢免官员。After the price of grain rose, the townspeople revolted and demanded the removal of the officials.
sceneCN: 这里 revolt 是「起义、反抗」（第 1 个义项：起来反对统治者）；句意：粮价上涨后，城里的居民起来反抗，要求罢免官员。

senses.title: Rising against a ruler
senses.definition: to take violent action against a government
senses.definitionCN: 对政府采取暴力行动
senses.example: The peasants revolted against the heavy taxes.
senses.exampleCN: 农民反抗沉重的赋税。
senses.why: The Latin root volv means to roll, as a crowd rolls against authority.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 volv 意为滚动，人群如浪潮般涌向权威。

senses.title: Strong disgust
senses.definition: to feel strong disgust at something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事感到强烈厌恶
senses.example: She revolted at the sight of the dirty kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 看到肮脏的厨房，她感到厌恶。
senses.why: The mind can turn away as violently as a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 内心的抗拒可以像人群一样激烈地转向。

senses.title: A rebellion
senses.definition: an act of rising against authority
senses.definitionCN: 反对权威的行动
senses.example: The revolt was crushed within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 这场起义一周内就被镇压了。
senses.why: The verb's action becomes a named event.
senses.whyCN: 动词的行为变成了一个有名称的事件。

intro.en: Revolt comes from French revolter, from Italian rivoltare, to turn over.
intro.cn: revolt 源自法语 revolter，再往前是意大利语 rivoltare（翻转）。

items.en: Revolvere joins re-, back, to volvere, to roll.
items.cn: revolvere 由 re-（回）与 volvere（滚）组成。

items.en: Rivoltare means to turn over or throw back.
items.cn: rivoltare 意为翻转或掷回。

items.en: Revolter brings the word into French.
items.cn: revolter 把词带入法语。

items.en: Revolt first means to turn away from a ruler.
items.cn: revolt 最初指背离统治者。

items.en: It also names the uprising itself.
items.cn: 它也指起义事件本身。

note.en: Revolt is a turning away; revolution is a full turning around.
note.cn: revolt 是转开，revolution 是彻底转一圈。

entries.definition: a handgun with a turning cylinder

normalIntro.en: Revolt is a crowd rolling back against authority.
normalIntro.cn: revolt 是人群掉头涌向权威。

normal.en: Revolt against a ruler means rise up.
normal.cn: revolt against a ruler 意为起来反抗。

normal.en: An armed revolt uses weapons.
normal.cn: an armed revolt 使用武器。

normal.en: Revolt at something means feel disgust.
normal.cn: revolt at something 意为感到厌恶。

normal.en: Crush a revolt means end it by force.
normal.cn: crush a revolt 意为以武力结束起义。

normal.en: Compare rebel: a rebel acts, a revolt is the rising.
normal.cn: 对比 rebel：rebel 指人行动，revolt 指起义本身。

abstract.en: Picture a flag turning against the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一面逆风翻卷的旗帜。

abstract.en: Imagine a wave rolling back toward the shore it came from.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪朝来时的岸边涌回。

abstract.en: Think of a door pushed shut by many hands at once.
abstract.cn: 想象许多只手同时把门推上。

examples.en: The workers revolted against the new rules.
examples.cn: 工人们反抗新规定。

examples.en: The smell made him revolt.
examples.cn: 那气味让他感到厌恶。

examples.en: The revolt spread through the northern towns.
examples.cn: 起义蔓延到北方城镇。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ volt（转）」——掉头转向权威，就是反抗、起义。

root: 拉丁语 revolvere（翻滚回去）＝ re-（回）＋ volvere（滚）→ 意大利语 rivoltare → 法语 revolter → revolt。

sensesIntro.en: Revolt begins as rising against a ruler, then describes inner disgust, and finally names the uprising itself.
sensesIntro.cn: revolt 先指起来反抗统治者，再描述内心的厌恶，最后指起义事件本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with raised hands and a flag in the wind.
core.cn: 核心意象：举手的人群与风中翻卷的旗帜。

branches.en: Rising against a ruler is the core.
branches.cn: 反抗统治者是核心含义。

branches.en: The mind turns away in disgust.
branches.cn: 内心因厌恶而转开。

branches.en: The rising becomes a named event.
branches.cn: 起义成为有名称的事件。

branches.en: The action and the event share one word.
branches.cn: 行为与事件共用一个词。

branches.en: Disgust and rebellion both mean turning away.
branches.cn: 厌恶与叛乱都意味着转开。

intro.en: Revolt combines re-, back, with the Latin root volv, to roll.
intro.cn: revolt 由 re-（回）与拉丁词根 volv（滚）组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere, to roll, explains the rolling movement of a crowd.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 volvere（滚）解释了人群如浪潮般的滚动。

items.example: Rivoltare brings the word toward French.
Revolter is the direct French source.
items.exampleCN: revolter 是直接的法语来源。
revolting 描述令人厌恶的事物。

latinEntries.exampleCN: volvere 是 revolve 与 revolt 的基础。
revolvere 发展出意大利语 rivoltare。

definition_en: a complete change in government or in the way something works
core_image: 旧雕像被拉倒，人群围着一面新旗帜
scene: 机器进入工厂后，纺织业经历了一场彻底的变革。After machines entered the factories, the textile industry went through a complete revolution.
sceneCN: 这里 revolution 是「彻底变革」（第 2 个义项：事物运作方式的巨变）；句意：机器进入工厂后，纺织业经历了一场彻底的变革。

senses.title: Political change
senses.definition: a complete change of government, often by force
senses.definitionCN: 通常以武力实现的政权彻底更替
senses.example: The revolution ended the old monarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 这场革命终结了旧君主制。
senses.why: Revolvere means to roll back; a political order is turned over.
senses.whyCN: revolvere 意为滚回，政治秩序被彻底翻转。

senses.title: Complete change
senses.definition: a great change in the way something works
senses.definitionCN: 事物运作方式的巨大变化
senses.example: The internet brought a revolution in communication.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网带来了通讯领域的巨变。
senses.why: The word moves from politics to technology and society.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从政治领域延伸到技术与社会。

senses.title: Turning motion
senses.definition: a circular movement around a center
senses.definitionCN: 绕中心的圆周运动
senses.example: One revolution of the wheel takes a second.
senses.exampleCN: 轮子转一圈用一秒。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the physical turning of a wheel.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的含义是轮子的物理转动。

intro.en: Revolution comes from Latin revolutio, a turning back, from revolvere.
intro.cn: revolution 源自拉丁语 revolutio（翻转），来自 revolvere。

items.en: Revolvere means to roll back.
items.cn: revolvere 意为滚回。

items.en: Revolutio names a rolling back or turning around.
items.cn: revolutio 指滚回或翻转。

items.en: French revolution carries the turning idea.
items.cn: 法语 revolution 保留了转动的含义。

items.en: Revolution first means a turning of a wheel.
items.cn: revolution 最初指轮子的转动。

items.en: It becomes a complete change of government.
items.cn: 它逐渐指政权的彻底更替。

note.en: Revolution is a full turn; revolt is a turning away.
note.cn: revolution 是整圈翻转；revolt 是转身反抗。

normalIntro.en: Revolution is the wheel of history turning a full circle.
normalIntro.cn: revolution 是历史之轮转过一整圈。

normal.en: The industrial revolution changed how people worked.
normal.cn: 工业革命改变了人们的工作方式。

normal.en: A revolution in medicine saved many lives.
normal.cn: 医学领域的革命挽救了许多生命。

normal.en: The wheel makes one revolution per second.
normal.cn: 轮子每秒转一圈。

normal.en: A political revolution replaces a government.
normal.cn: 政治革命更替政府。

normal.en: Compare revolt: revolt is a rising, revolution is a full change.
normal.cn: 对比 revolt：revolt 是起义，revolution 是彻底的变革。

abstract.en: Picture a statue falling and a new flag rising.
abstract.cn: 想象雕像倒下、新旗升起。

abstract.en: Imagine a wheel spinning once around its axle.
abstract.cn: 想象轮子绕轴转了一整圈。

abstract.en: Think of a map redrawn from top to bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张从头到尾重新绘制的地图。

examples.en: The revolution changed the country for ever.
examples.cn: 这场革命永远地改变了这个国家。

examples.en: Plastic caused a revolution in daily life.
examples.cn: 塑料在日常生活中引发了一场变革。

examples.en: The engine runs at three thousand revolutions per minute.
examples.cn: 这台发动机每分钟转三千圈。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ volution（转）」——转一整圈，就是旋转、革命。

root: 拉丁语 revolvere（滚回）→ revolutio（翻转）→ 法语 revolution → revolution，核心义「整圈翻转」。

sensesIntro.en: Revolution starts with political overthrow, extends to any complete change, and keeps the physical sense of one full turn.
sensesIntro.cn: revolution 从政治推翻开始，延伸到任何彻底变革，同时保留转一整圈的物理含义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fallen statue, a new flag and a turning wheel.
core.cn: 核心意象：倒下的雕像、新的旗帜与转动的巨轮。

branches.en: Political overthrow is the public sense.
branches.cn: 政治推翻是公共层面的含义。

branches.en: Any deep change can be called a revolution.
branches.cn: 任何深刻变化都能称为革命。

branches.en: One full turn keeps the oldest meaning.
branches.cn: 整圈转动保留了最古老的含义。

branches.en: Politics and technology both turn the old order over.
branches.cn: 政治与技术都翻转了旧秩序。

branches.en: A wheel and a government can both turn around.
branches.cn: 轮子与政权都能转过来。

intro.en: Revolution combines re-, back, the root volv, to roll, and the noun suffix -ion.
intro.cn: revolution 由 re-（回）、词根 volv（滚）与名词后缀 -ion 组成。

latinIntro.en: Latin revolvere and revolutio give the word its full shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 revolvere 与 revolutio 赋予这个词完整形态。

items.meaning: a gun with a turning part
items.example: Revolver comes from the same turning root.
items.exampleCN: revolver 来自同一个表示转动的词根。

latinEntries.example: Revolvere leads to the noun revolutio.

definition_en: something given in return for good work or help
core_image: 一只摊开的手掌上放着一枚发亮的金币
scene: 找回走失的小狗后，主人给了邻居一笔酬谢。After the lost dog was found, the owner gave the neighbor a reward.
sceneCN: 这里 reward 是「酬谢、报酬」（第 1 个义项：为帮助而给的回报）；句意：找回走失的小狗后，主人给了邻居一笔酬谢。

senses.title: Something given back
senses.definition: something given for good work or help
senses.definitionCN: 因出色工作或帮助而给予的东西
senses.example: A reward was offered for the missing ring.
senses.exampleCN: 有人悬赏寻找丢失的戒指。
senses.why: The word joins re-, back, with a French root meaning to regard.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 re-（回）与表示注视的法语词根组成。

senses.title: A good result
senses.definition: a benefit that comes from an effort
senses.definitionCN: 努力带来的好处
senses.example: Hard work brings its own reward.
senses.exampleCN: 努力本身就会带来回报。
senses.why: What returns to you after effort is also a reward.
senses.whyCN: 努力之后回到你身边的东西也是回报。

senses.title: To give a reward
senses.definition: to give something for good work
senses.definitionCN: 因出色工作而给予某物
senses.example: The school rewarded the best students.
senses.exampleCN: 学校奖励了最优秀的学生。
senses.why: The noun's action becomes a verb.
senses.whyCN: 名词所指的行为变成动词。

intro.en: Reward comes from Old French rewarder, to regard, related to regard.
intro.cn: reward 源自法语 rewarder（注视、看待），与 regard 同源。

items.en: Rewarder means to regard or consider.
items.cn: rewarder 意为注视或看待。

items.en: The prefix re- adds a sense of return.
items.cn: 前缀 re- 加上返回的含义。

items.en: Reward first means to regard with favour.
items.cn: reward 最初指以赞许的目光看待。

items.en: It becomes something given in return.
items.cn: 它变成回赠之物。

items.en: It also means the benefit of effort.
items.cn: 它也指努力带来的好处。

note.en: Reward returns something for effort; a prize is won in a contest.
note.cn: reward 因付出而回赠；prize 是在比赛中赢得的奖品。

normalIntro.en: Reward is what comes back to you after good work.
normalIntro.cn: reward 是出色工作之后回到你身边的东西。

normal.en: A reward was offered for the lost cat.
normal.cn: 有人悬赏寻找走失的猫。

normal.en: Financial reward means money for good work.
normal.cn: financial reward 意为因工作出色而得到的钱。

normal.en: Hard work brings its own reward.
normal.cn: 努力本身就会带来回报。

normal.en: The school rewarded the best students.
normal.cn: 学校奖励了最优秀的学生。

normal.en: Compare award: an award is official, a reward returns a favour.
normal.cn: 对比 award：award 是正式奖项，reward 是对帮助的回赠。

abstract.en: Picture a coin shining on an open palm.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚金币在摊开的手掌上发亮。

abstract.en: Imagine a garden giving fruit after long care.
abstract.cn: 想象花园在长期照料后结出果实。

abstract.en: Think of a bell that rings back when you call.
abstract.cn: 想象你呼唤时回响的钟声。

examples.en: The company gave him a reward for his idea.
examples.cn: 公司因他的想法给了他奖励。

examples.en: The reward for patience is often trust.
examples.cn: 耐心的回报往往是信任。

examples.en: They rewarded the volunteers with a dinner.
examples.cn: 他们用一顿晚餐酬谢志愿者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）＋ ward（看守、注视）」——因表现好而回赠给你的东西，就是奖励。

root: 古法语 rewarder（关注、酬报）＝ re-（回）＋ warder（看守）→ reward，核心义「回赠、回报」。

sensesIntro.en: Reward is something given back for help, then the benefit of effort, and finally the verb for giving it.
sensesIntro.cn: reward 先是因帮助而回赠之物，再指努力的益处，最后作动词表示给予奖励。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shining coin resting on an open palm.
core.cn: 核心意象：摊开的手掌上放着一枚发亮的金币。

branches.en: A gift for help is the core sense.
branches.cn: 因帮助而给的礼物是核心含义。

branches.en: Effort itself can bring a reward.
branches.cn: 努力本身也能带来回报。

branches.en: The verb gives the reward.
branches.cn: 动词表示给予奖励。

branches.en: A gift and a benefit both return to the giver.
branches.cn: 礼物与益处都回到付出者身上。

branches.en: The noun and verb share one action.
branches.cn: 名词与动词共用一个行为。

intro.en: Reward joins re-, back, to a French root meaning to guard or regard.
intro.cn: reward 由 re-（回）与表示看守、注视的法语词根组成。

latinIntro.en: The word comes through Old French rather than directly from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是经古法语传入的，而非直接来自拉丁语。

items.exampleCN: rewardingly 描述某事结束的方式。

definition_en: a regular pattern of sounds or movements
core_image: 鼓面上一圈圈震动的波纹
scene: 鼓手让鼓点保持稳定的节奏，舞者跟着脚步移动。The drummer kept a steady rhythm, and the dancers moved with the beat.
sceneCN: 这里 rhythm 是「节奏」（第 1 个义项：声音有规律的重复）；句意：鼓手让鼓点保持稳定的节奏，舞者跟着脚步移动。

senses.title: Sound pattern
senses.definition: a regular repeated pattern of sound
senses.definitionCN: 声音有规律的重复模式
senses.example: The song has a fast rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌节奏很快。
senses.why: The Greek word rhythmos means measured flow.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 rhythmos 意为有节制的流动。

senses.title: Regular movement
senses.definition: a regular pattern of movement
senses.definitionCN: 动作的有规律重复
senses.example: The rowers found a common rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 划桨手找到了共同的节奏。
senses.why: Any repeated motion can be called a rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 任何重复的动作都可称为节奏。

senses.title: Daily pattern
senses.definition: a regular way in which things happen
senses.definitionCN: 事物有规律的发生方式
senses.example: Her days follow a calm rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 她的日子遵循平静的规律。
senses.why: The idea spreads from music to the pattern of life.
senses.whyCN: 这一概念从音乐延伸到生活规律。

intro.en: Rhythm comes from Greek rhythmos, measured motion, from rhein, to flow.
intro.cn: rhythm 源自希腊语 rhythmos（有节制的运动），来自 rhein（流动）。

items.en: Rhythmos means measured flow.
items.cn: rhythmos 意为有节制的流动。

items.en: Rhein means to flow.
items.cn: rhein 意为流动。

items.en: Rhythmus keeps the Greek form.
items.cn: rhythmus 保留了希腊语形式。

items.en: French rithme shapes the spelling.
items.cn: 法语 rithme 塑造了拼写。

items.en: Rhythm loses some Greek letters but keeps the beat.
items.cn: rhythm 丢掉了部分希腊字母，却保留了节拍。

note.en: Rhythm is the pattern; a beat is one pulse inside it.
note.cn: rhythm 是整体模式；beat 是其中一个脉冲。

entries.definition: one hit in a regular series
the speed of a piece of music

normalIntro.en: Rhythm is the heartbeat of music and of days.
normalIntro.cn: rhythm 是音乐与日子的心跳。

normal.en: A steady rhythm keeps dancers together.
normal.cn: 稳定的节奏让舞者整齐一致。

normal.en: The song has a lively rhythm.
normal.cn: 这首歌节奏活泼。

normal.en: Body rhythm changes when we are tired.
normal.cn: 疲倦时身体节律会改变。

normal.en: Keep the rhythm means do not speed up.
normal.cn: keep the rhythm 意为不要加速。

normal.en: Compare beat: a beat is one hit, a rhythm is the whole pattern.
normal.cn: 对比 beat：beat 是一下敲击，rhythm 是整个模式。

abstract.en: Picture ripples spreading from a drum.
abstract.cn: 想象鼓面上一圈圈扩散的波纹。

abstract.en: Imagine waves meeting the shore at equal intervals.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪以相等间隔拍岸。

abstract.en: Think of a clock ticking inside a song.
abstract.cn: 想象歌声里有一只钟在滴答走动。

examples.en: The drummer lost the rhythm for a moment.
examples.cn: 鼓手有一瞬间失去了节奏。

examples.en: Her writing has a natural rhythm.
examples.cn: 她的文字有自然的韵律。

examples.en: The city has its own daily rhythm.
examples.cn: 这座城市有自己的日常节奏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rhythm」中间只有一个元音——把单词当作鼓点来记：六个字母，两拍落下。

root: 希腊语 rhythmos（有节制的流动）← rhein（流动）→ 拉丁语 rhythmus → 法语 rithme → rhythm。

sensesIntro.en: Rhythm begins as a pattern of sound, extends to repeated movement, and finally to the regular pattern of daily life.
sensesIntro.cn: rhythm 从声音模式开始，延伸到重复的动作，最后指日常生活的规律。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: ripples spreading from a drumhead.
core.cn: 核心意象：鼓面上一圈圈扩散的波纹。

branches.en: Sound is the first home of rhythm.
branches.cn: 声音是节奏最初的家。

branches.en: Repeated movement carries the same pattern.
branches.cn: 重复的动作承载同样的模式。

branches.en: Daily life also has a regular beat.
branches.cn: 日常生活也有规律的节拍。

branches.en: Music and motion share one pattern.
branches.cn: 音乐与动作共用一个模式。

branches.en: Bodies and days both repeat in time.
branches.cn: 身体与日子都在时间中重复。

intro.en: Rhythm carries the Greek root rhy, meaning to flow.
intro.cn: rhythm 带有希腊词根 rhy，意为流动。

latinIntro.en: Greek rhythmos passed into Latin as rhythmus.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 rhythmos 以 rhythmus 的形式进入拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: Rhythmus carries the Greek word into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rhythmus 把希腊词带入拉丁语。

definition_en: a white grain used as food, grown in wet fields
core_image: 竹筐里堆着雪白的米粒，旁边是一株稻穗
scene: 南方的水田里，农民弯腰插秧，等到秋天收割稻谷。In the wet fields of the south, farmers bend to plant rice and harvest the grain in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 rice 是「稻、稻谷」（第 1 个义项：生长在水田中的作物）；句意：南方的水田里，农民弯腰插秧，等到秋天收割稻谷。

senses.title: The plant
senses.definition: a grass plant grown in wet fields
senses.definitionCN: 生长在水田中的禾本科植物
senses.example: Rice grows best in warm, wet fields.
senses.exampleCN: 稻子在温暖湿润的水田里长得最好。
senses.why: The word names the living plant before the food.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先指活着的植物，再指食物。

senses.title: The grain
senses.definition: the white grain taken from the plant
senses.definitionCN: 从植株上收获的白色谷粒
senses.example: The shop sells rice by the kilo.
senses.exampleCN: 商店按公斤卖大米。
senses.why: The harvested grain keeps the same name.
senses.whyCN: 收获的谷粒沿用同一名称。

senses.title: Cooked food
senses.definition: the grain cooked and eaten
senses.definitionCN: 煮熟后食用的米粒
senses.example: We had rice with fish for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 我们晚餐吃了米饭配鱼。
senses.why: Cooked grain on a plate is the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 盘中的熟米是日常含义。

intro.en: Rice comes from Greek oryza through Latin, Italian and French.
intro.cn: rice 从希腊语 oryza 经拉丁语、意大利语和法语传来。

items.en: Oryza names the grain.
items.cn: oryza 指这种谷物。

items.en: Oryza keeps the Greek word.
items.cn: oryza 保留了希腊词。

items.en: Riso shortens the Latin form.
items.cn: riso 缩短了拉丁语形式。

items.en: Ris enters Old French.
items.cn: ris 进入古法语。

items.en: Rice settles as the modern English form.
items.cn: rice 定型为现代英语形式。

note.en: Rice is the grain; a paddy is the field where it grows.
note.cn: rice 是谷物；paddy 是种它的水田。

entries.definition: a small hard seed used as food

normalIntro.en: Rice is the white grain that feeds half the world.
normalIntro.cn: rice 是养活半个世界的白色谷粒。

normal.en: Rice grows in wet fields.
normal.cn: 稻子生长在水田里。

normal.en: A bowl of rice is served with dinner.
normal.cn: 晚餐配一碗米饭。

normal.en: A rice field is a field for rice.
normal.cn: rice field 是种稻的田。

normal.en: Cooked rice is soft and white.
normal.cn: 煮熟的米饭柔软洁白。

normal.en: Compare paddy: a paddy is the field, rice is the crop.
normal.cn: 对比 paddy：paddy 是田，rice 是作物。

abstract.en: Picture a white bowl filled with tiny grains.
abstract.cn: 想象一只装满细小米粒的白碗。

abstract.en: Imagine a field of green stalks reflected in water.
abstract.cn: 想象绿色的稻秆倒映在水中。

abstract.en: Think of a table where one grain feeds many hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，一种谷物养活许多双手。

examples.en: Rice is the main food in many countries.
examples.cn: 稻米是许多国家的主食。

examples.en: They plant rice in May.
examples.cn: 他们在五月插秧。

examples.en: She cooked rice for lunch.
examples.cn: 她做了米饭当午饭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rice」与「rise（升起）」只差一个字母——稻子在水田里一天天长高。

root: 希腊语 oryza（稻米）→ 拉丁语 oryza → 意大利语 riso → 古法语 ris → rice。

sensesIntro.en: Rice names the plant, the grain, and the cooked food in turn.
sensesIntro.cn: rice 依次指稻株、大米和米饭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: white grains in a bamboo basket beside a rice stalk.
core.cn: 核心意象：竹筐里的白米与旁边的稻穗。

branches.en: The plant is the starting sense.
branches.cn: 稻株是起始含义。

branches.en: The harvested grain keeps the name.
branches.cn: 收获的谷粒沿用这个名字。

branches.en: Cooked rice is the food on the table.
branches.cn: 米饭是桌上的食物。

branches.en: Plant and grain are one crop.
branches.cn: 植株与谷粒是同一作物。

branches.en: The grain becomes food after cooking.
branches.cn: 谷粒煮熟后成为食物。

intro.en: Rice comes from Greek through Latin, Italian and French.
intro.cn: rice 从希腊语经拉丁语、意大利语和法语传来。

latinIntro.en: Latin oryza is the pivot between Greek and the modern forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 oryza 是希腊语与现代形式之间的枢纽。

items.example: Ris is the Old French form.
A ricer presses food into rice-like pieces.
items.exampleCN: 压泥器把食物压成米粒状。
ricey 描述类似米的味道。

latinEntries.example: Oryza passes from Greek into Latin.
latinEntries.exampleCN: oryza 从希腊语进入拉丁语。

definition_en: so silly or unreasonable that it deserves laughter
core_image: 戴着过大的帽子去开会的人
scene: 他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。He wore a huge hat to the meeting and looked ridiculous.
sceneCN: 这里 ridiculous 是「可笑的」（第 1 个义项：荒谬到引人发笑）；句意：他戴着一顶过大的帽子走进会场，看上去十分可笑。

senses.title: Too silly to believe
senses.definition: so silly that it seems impossible
senses.definitionCN: 愚蠢得让人觉得不可能
senses.example: It is ridiculous to blame the rain for your lateness.
senses.exampleCN: 把迟到归咎于下雨实在荒谬。
senses.why: The word comes from laughter at what is absurd.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于对荒谬之事的发笑。

senses.title: Funny to look at
senses.definition: strange enough to make people laugh
senses.definitionCN: 古怪得令人发笑
senses.example: He looked ridiculous in that tiny jacket.
senses.exampleCN: 他穿着那件小小的外套显得很可笑。
senses.why: Something badly matched looks laughable.
senses.whyCN: 搭配不当的东西看起来就好笑。

senses.title: Wildly unreasonable
senses.definition: unreasonably large or small
senses.definitionCN: 大小得极不合理
senses.example: They asked a ridiculous price for the old bike.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为那辆旧自行车要了个离谱的价钱。
senses.why: A number beyond sense also earns a laugh.
senses.whyCN: 不合常理的数字同样引人发笑。

intro.en: Ridiculous comes from Latin ridiculus, laughable, from ridere, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 源自拉丁语 ridiculus（可笑的），来自 ridere（笑）。

items.en: Ridere means to laugh.
items.cn: ridere 意为笑。

items.en: Ridiculus means fit to be laughed at.
items.cn: ridiculus 意为值得被嘲笑的。

items.en: French ridicule carries the sense of mockery.
items.cn: 法语 ridicule 带有嘲弄之意。

items.en: English ridiculous means absurd.
items.cn: 英语 ridiculous 意为荒谬。

items.en: It also scolds wild prices and plans.
items.cn: 如今它也用来批评离谱的价格与计划。

note.en: Ridiculous points to laughter; absurd points to the lack of sense.
note.cn: ridiculous 指向发笑，absurd 指向缺乏道理。

entries.definition: so bad or odd that one laughs

normalIntro.en: Ridiculous describes what deserves a laugh.
normalIntro.cn: ridiculous 形容值得发笑的事。

normal.en: Ridicule is the verb that mocks.
normal.cn: ridicule 是表示嘲笑的动词。

normal.en: A ridiculous idea makes no sense.
normal.cn: ridiculous idea 毫无道理。

normal.en: That hat looks ridiculous on you.
normal.cn: 那顶帽子戴在你头上很可笑。

normal.en: A ridiculous price is far too high.
normal.cn: ridiculous price 高得离谱。

normal.en: Laughter is hidden inside the word.
normal.cn: 笑声藏在这个词里面。

abstract.en: Picture a clown at a serious meeting.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小丑出现在严肃的会议上。

abstract.en: Imagine shoes three sizes too big.
abstract.cn: 想象一双大了三号的鞋。

abstract.en: Think of a price tag with too many zeros.
abstract.cn: 想象一张写着太多零的价签。

examples.en: The plan sounded ridiculous at first.
examples.cn: 这个计划起初听起来很荒唐。

examples.en: It is ridiculous to walk in this storm.
examples.cn: 在这种暴风雨里走路太荒唐了。

examples.en: She felt ridiculous in the wrong uniform.
examples.cn: 穿着错误的制服让她觉得很可笑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ridi（笑）＋ culous」——让人忍不住笑出来的，就是荒谬可笑。

root: 拉丁语 ridere（笑）→ ridiculus（可笑的）→ 法语 ridicule → ridiculous，核心义「荒谬到引人发笑」。

sensesIntro.en: Ridiculous means silly enough to laugh at, funny in appearance, or wildly unreasonable.
sensesIntro.cn: ridiculous 意为愚蠢可笑、模样古怪，或离谱得不合理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a laugh rising at something absurd.
core.cn: 核心意象：面对荒谬之事升起的笑声。

branches.en: An absurd idea invites laughter.
branches.cn: 荒谬的想法招来笑声。

branches.en: A mismatched outfit looks funny.
branches.cn: 不搭的装扮看起来好笑。

branches.en: A wild price is laughably unreasonable.
branches.cn: 离谱的价格荒唐得可笑。

branches.en: Both a foolish plan and a strange look make us laugh.
branches.cn: 愚蠢的计划与古怪的模样都让人发笑。

branches.en: A funny look and a wild price both break good sense.
branches.cn: 古怪模样与离谱价格都违背常理。

intro.en: Ridiculous grows from the Latin root rid, to laugh.
intro.cn: ridiculous 由拉丁词根 rid（笑）生长而来。

latinIntro.en: Ridere gives ridiculus, and French carries ridicule into English.
latinIntro.cn: ridere 给出 ridiculus，法语又把 ridicule 带进英语。

items.example: Rid carries the idea of laughter.
Ridicule brings the word to English.

latinEntries.example: Ridere is the source of ridiculous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ridere 是 ridiculous 的来源。

definition_zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的
definition_en: stiff and unable to bend, or strict and unwilling to change
core_image: 一根弯不动的旧金属管
scene: 这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。The old pipe had become rigid and cracked when bent.
sceneCN: 这里 rigid 是「僵硬的」（第 1 个义项：坚硬而无法弯曲）；句意：这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。

pos.zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的

senses.title: Stiff to the touch
senses.definition: hard and not able to bend
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬且不能弯曲
senses.example: The frame is made of rigid steel.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由坚硬的钢材制成。
senses.why: Rigid begins as the Latin word for stiff.
senses.whyCN: rigid 最初就是拉丁语中表示僵硬的那个词。

senses.title: Strict and fixed
senses.definition: not allowing change or flexibility
senses.definitionCN: 不允许改变或变通
senses.example: The school has rigid rules about phones.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对手机有严格的规定。
senses.why: A rule that cannot bend is rigid.
senses.whyCN: 不能变通的规则就是僵硬的。

senses.title: Frozen with feeling
senses.definition: unable to move because of fear or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧或震惊而无法动弹
senses.example: He stood rigid at the edge of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 他僵立在悬崖边。
senses.why: The body turns stiff when terror takes over.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧占据身心时，身体会变得僵硬。

intro.en: Rigid comes from Latin rigidus, stiff, from rigere, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 源自拉丁语 rigidus（僵硬），来自 rigere（变硬）。

items.en: Rigere means to be stiff.
items.cn: rigere 意为僵硬。

items.en: Rigidus means stiff or unbending.
items.cn: rigidus 意为僵硬、不弯。

items.en: French rigide keeps the physical sense.
items.cn: 法语 rigide 保留了物理含义。

items.en: English rigid adds the sense of strict rules.
items.cn: 英语 rigid 增加了严格规则的含义。

items.en: It also describes a body frozen by fear.
items.cn: 它也形容因恐惧而僵住的身体。

note.en: Rigid is stiff in body or rule; strict is firm about rules only.
note.cn: rigid 可指身体或规则僵硬，strict 只强调规则严格。

normalIntro.en: Rigid is a rod that refuses to bend.
normalIntro.cn: rigid 就是一根拒绝弯曲的杆子。

normal.en: Rigid rules leave no room to bend.
normal.cn: rigid rules 不留变通余地。

normal.en: A rigid frame holds its shape.
normal.cn: rigid frame 保持自身形状。

normal.en: Rigid material does not fold.
normal.cn: rigid material 不会折叠。

normal.en: Rigid with fear means frozen still.
normal.cn: rigid with fear 意为吓得僵住。

normal.en: Rigidity is the noun of rigid.
normal.cn: rigidity 是 rigid 的名词形式。

abstract.en: Picture a steel bar under heavy load.
abstract.cn: 想象一根承重的钢条。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier standing without a twitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一名士兵一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Think of a frozen branch snapping in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象冻硬的树枝在风中折断。

examples.en: The tent poles are light but rigid.
examples.cn: 帐篷杆又轻又硬。

examples.en: His rigid attitude made talk difficult.
examples.cn: 他死板的态度让谈话很难进行。

examples.en: She sat rigid with shock.
examples.cn: 她震惊得僵坐在那里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rigid」听起来像「硬紧的」——又硬又紧，弯都弯不动。

root: 拉丁语 rigere（变硬）→ rigidus（僵硬的）→ rigid，核心义「硬得无法弯曲，因而不能变通」。

sensesIntro.en: Rigid means physically stiff, strictly fixed, or frozen by strong feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: rigid 意为物理上僵硬、规则上严格固定，或因强烈情绪而僵住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rod that will not bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯不动的杆子。

branches.en: Physical stiffness is the root sense.
branches.cn: 物理僵硬是根本义项。

branches.en: A rule that cannot bend becomes rigid.
branches.cn: 不能变通的规则变得僵死。

branches.en: Fear freezes the body into stiffness.
branches.cn: 恐惧把身体冻得僵硬。

branches.en: Stiff steel and stiff rules share one image.
branches.cn: 坚硬的钢与僵硬的规则共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Metal and muscles both lose their give.
branches.cn: 金属与肌肉都失去了弹性。

intro.en: Rigid comes from the Latin root rig, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 来自拉丁词根 rig（僵硬）。

latinIntro.en: Rigere gives rigidus, and French rigide carries it to English.
latinIntro.cn: rigere 给出 rigidus，法语 rigide 把它带入英语。

items.example: Rig carries the idea of stiffness.

latinEntries.example: Rigidus is the source of rigid.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rigidus 是 rigid 的来源。

definition_zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严苛的；严酷的
definition_en: carried out with great care and strict standards, leaving no step unchecked
core_image: 实验室里每份样本都要两个人各自核对，记录上少一行就整批重做
scene: 实验室里，每一批样本都要两人分别核对，任何一步记录不全就得重做。The trial's rigorous protocol required two independent checks for every sample.
sceneCN: 这里指标准严格、不留缺口（第 1 个义项：严格而彻底的）；句意为该试验的严谨规程要求每份样本都做两次独立核对。图中可辨识物件：样本架、双人核对表、签名栏、重做标记。

pos.zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严酷的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地；严谨地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严格；严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷；严谨」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「坚硬的；僵化的」
由「僵硬的」加名词尾构成，义为「刚性；僵化」

senses.title: Strict and thorough
senses.definition: done with great care and with no step left unchecked
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的仔细进行，每一步都被核查
senses.example: The safety review was rigorous, and nothing was signed off on trust.
senses.exampleCN: 安全审查十分严格，没有任何一项是靠信任签字的。
senses.why: The Latin root means stiffness, and a stiff procedure does not bend to convenience.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「僵硬」，僵硬的程序不会为图方便而弯折。

senses.title: Demanding testing
senses.definition: testing carried out under hard, controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在严苛且有控制的条件下进行的测试
senses.example: The battery underwent rigorous testing at high and low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在高温与低温下接受了严苛测试。
senses.why: Tests are rigorous when the conditions are harder than ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 当条件比日常使用更苛刻，测试就是严苛的。

senses.title: A proof with no gaps
senses.definition: a proof in which every step is justified
senses.definitionCN: 每一步都有依据的证明
senses.example: A rigorous proof does not rely on a diagram that merely looks right.
senses.exampleCN: 严密的证明不依赖一张只是看起来正确的图。
senses.why: In mathematics the word means the argument cannot be loosened anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 在数学里，这个词意味着论证在任何一处都不能放松。

senses.title: Hard training
senses.definition: training that is physically or mentally severe
senses.definitionCN: 在体力或心力上都很艰苦的训练
senses.example: Rigorous training prepared the crew for a month at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 严酷的训练让船员为海上一个月做好了准备。
senses.why: Training borrows the word because a strict method also trains the will.
senses.whyCN: 训练借用这个词，因为严格的方法也在训练意志。

senses.title: Standards without shortcuts
senses.definition: standards that admit no exceptions for convenience
senses.definitionCN: 不为方便开例外口子的标准
senses.example: The journal applies rigorous standards to every submission, even invited ones.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊对每篇投稿都适用严格标准，受邀稿也不例外。
senses.why: A standard is rigorous when the exception costs more than the rule.
senses.whyCN: 当例外的代价高于规则，标准才是严格的。

senses.title: Analysis that checks its assumptions
senses.definition: analysis that tests its own assumptions rather than assuming them
senses.definitionCN: 检验自身假设、而不是直接假定成立的分析
senses.example: A rigorous analysis of the survey must first ask who was not asked.
senses.exampleCN: 对这项调查的严谨分析，首先要问谁没有被问到。
senses.why: The analysis turns the strictness on itself, which is the highest form of the method.
senses.whyCN: 分析把严格对准自身，这是该方法最高的形态。

senses.title: Selection by hard tests
senses.definition: choosing only those who pass demanding tests
senses.definitionCN: 只让通过高要求测试者入选
senses.example: The fellowship uses a rigorous selection process with three rounds of review.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金采用三轮评审的严格筛选流程。
senses.why: Selection is rigorous when the gate, not the label, does the choosing.
senses.whyCN: 当做出选择的是门槛而不是标签，筛选才是严格的。

senses.title: Enforcement without leniency
senses.definition: applying a rule fully, with no relaxed exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 完整执行规则，不作宽松的例外
senses.example: Rigorous enforcement of the smoking ban changed behaviour within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟规定的严格执行在一个月内改变了行为。
senses.why: Enforcement completes the word: the rule now has hands as well as words.
senses.whyCN: 执行补全了这个词：规则如今不光有条文，还有手。

intro.en: Rigorous comes from Latin rigor, stiffness or hardness, from rigere, to be stiff, with an adjective ending that reached English through French. The physical stiffness became a moral and methodological one: a standard that will not bend. The same root also gives rigid and rigor mortis.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 rigor「僵硬、坚硬」，出自 rigere「僵直」，加形容词尾后经法语进入英语。身体上的僵硬变成了道德与方法的僵硬：不肯弯折的标准。同一词根还给出 rigid 与「尸僵」一语。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff or numb, said of limbs and of cold.
items.cn: 这个词意为僵直、麻木，用于肢体，也用于寒冷。

items.en: Rigor named stiffness, hardness and, by extension, severity of rule or climate.
items.cn: 这个词指僵硬、坚硬，并引申指规则或气候的严酷。

items.en: Later Latin formed an adjective meaning full of stiffness or severity.
items.cn: 后起拉丁语构成形容词，意为「充满僵硬或严酷的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into the language of law and method.
items.cn: 法语把该形容词带入法律与方法的语言。

items.en: English applied it to rules, proofs and training.
items.cn: 英语把它用于规则、证明与训练。

items.en: Research methods fixed phrases such as rigorous testing; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 科研方法固定了「严苛测试」等说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stiffness root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of strictness. The note warns that vigorous looks like a relative but comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「僵硬」词根或形近；第二组指其他「严格」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「精力充沛」一词出自另一词根，并非同族。

entries.definition: Strictness or severity, and in medicine, a chill.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格或严酷，医学上指寒战。

entries.definition: Stiff and unable to bend, literally or in attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 指僵硬不能弯，字面或态度上皆可。

entries.definition: In a strict and thorough way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格而彻底的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being strict and thorough.
Full of energy and strength; its root means to be lively, not stiff.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、强健；其词根意为「有生气」，并非「僵硬」。

entries.definition: Insisting on exact obedience to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持对规则的精确遵守。

entries.definition: Complete, with no part left out.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整、没有遗漏任何部分。

entries.definition: Showing extreme attention to small details.
Tight and demanding, often of rules or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧而苛刻，多用于规则或条件。

entries.definition: Demanding a great deal of effort or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求大量努力或精确。
指在力度或对待上严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two signature lines, the frozen joint, the long proof and the three-round review.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两行签名、冻僵的关节、冗长的证明与三轮评审。

normal.en: A rigorous process has two signatures where one would do.
normal.cn: 严谨的流程在一个签名够用的地方放两个。

normal.en: Rigid means the joint will not bend; rigorous means the rule will not bend.
normal.cn: 「僵硬的」说关节不弯，「严格的」说规则不弯。

normal.en: A rigorous proof leaves no step to the reader's goodwill.
normal.cn: 严密的证明不把任何一步留给读者的善意。

normal.en: Rigorous training is remembered in the body, not in the notes.
normal.cn: 严酷的训练被记在身体里，而不是记在笔记里。

normal.en: Vigorous is about energy and rigorous is about stiffness, though they sound alike.
normal.cn: 「强健的」讲精力，「严格的」讲僵硬，尽管读音相似。

abstract.en: Strictness is a promise that the result will not depend on who was watching.
abstract.cn: 严格是一种承诺：结果不取决于当时谁在看。

abstract.en: The same stiffness that protects a result can freeze a field for a generation.
abstract.cn: 保护结果的那种僵硬，也可能把一个领域冻住一代人。

abstract.en: A rigorous standard is expensive, which is why it is often replaced by its description.
abstract.cn: 严格的标准很贵，所以常被它的描述所取代。

examples.en: The claim survived rigorous testing by three independent laboratories.
examples.cn: 这一主张经受了三家独立实验室的严苛测试。

examples.en: Her analysis was rigorous, and it questioned the survey's own assumptions.
examples.cn: 她的分析很严谨，也质疑了调查自身的假设。

examples.en: Rigorous enforcement, not new rules, reduced the accident rate.
examples.cn: 降低事故率的是严格执行，而不是新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞格若斯」：规矩「硬」得像冻住的关节，一步也不肯弯，检查才做得严

root: 源于拉丁语表示「僵直」的动词，其名词义为「僵硬、严酷」，后起形容词再经法语进入英语。同族有表示「严格」「僵硬的」「刚性」的词；形近而表示「精力充沛」的词出自表示「有生气」的另一词根。十六世纪进入英语；各技术短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn stiffness into method: a thorough procedure, demanding tests, gapless proofs, hard training, standards without shortcuts, self-checking analysis, strict selection, and full enforcement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「僵硬」变成方法：彻底的流程、严苛的测试、无缺口的证明、艰苦的训练、不许走捷径的标准、自查假设的分析、严格筛选与完整执行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on every sheet, and a whole batch is redone if one line is missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：每张记录上两个签名，少一行就整批重做。

branches.en: THE STIFF PROCEDURE: care that refuses convenience in every ordinary step.
branches.cn: 僵硬的程序：在每个寻常步骤上都不为方便让步。

branches.en: THE HARD TEST AND THE HARD DRILL: strict conditions, and training built under them.
branches.cn: 严苛的测试与艰苦的训练：严格的条件，以及在条件下筑起的训练。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ARGUMENT: proofs and analyses with no step left to goodwill.
branches.cn: 封闭的论证：不把任何一步留给善意的证明与分析。

branches.en: THE UNBENDING RULE: standards and enforcement that admit no exceptions.
branches.cn: 不肯弯的规则：不容例外开的标准与执行。

branches.en: THE NARROW GATE: selection that only lets the tested through.
branches.cn: 窄门：只让过关者进入的筛选。

intro.en: Rigorous is a Latin stiffness noun with an adjective ending; its family covers rigidity, strictness and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「僵硬」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖刚性、严格与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rigere and rigor supply the stiffness, and the later adjective rigorosus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「僵直」与「僵硬」提供词干，后起形容词给出英语形态。

items.example: The oldest root of the family.
It gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语形容词的形态。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
A same-root word from a different form.
items.exampleCN: 同词根但由另一形式构成的词。

items.example: Built on rigid, not on rigorous.
items.exampleCN: 由「僵硬的」构成，而非由本词构成。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「僵硬的」

definition_zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极其好笑的人或事；参与暴乱
definition_en: a violent public disturbance, or something very funny
core_image: 深夜广场上混乱的人群
scene: 广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。The riot in the square only calmed down late at night.
sceneCN: 这里 riot 是「骚乱」（第 1 个义项：公众场所的暴力混乱）；句意：广场上的骚乱直到深夜才慢慢平息。

pos.zh: 暴乱；骚乱；极好笑的人或事

senses.title: A violent crowd
senses.definition: a violent disturbance by a crowd in public
senses.definitionCN: 人群在公共场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: The riot broke out after the match.
senses.exampleCN: 比赛结束后爆发了骚乱。
senses.why: A crowd that loses control becomes a riot.
senses.whyCN: 失去控制的人群就成了骚乱。

senses.title: Very funny
senses.definition: a person or thing that is very funny
senses.definitionCN: 非常滑稽的人或事
senses.example: His story was an absolute riot.
senses.exampleCN: 他的故事实在太逗了。
senses.why: Wild laughter feels like a small riot.
senses.whyCN: 狂笑的感觉就像一场小小的骚动。

senses.title: To join a riot
senses.definition: to take part in a violent public disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 参与公众场所的暴力骚乱
senses.example: Crowds rioted outside the old factory.
senses.exampleCN: 人群在旧工厂外暴动。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为行为本身。

intro.en: Riot comes from Old French riote, a quarrel or wild behaviour.
intro.cn: riot 源自古法语 riote，意为争吵或放荡行为。

items.en: Riote means a quarrel.
items.cn: riote 意为争吵。

items.en: The word also suggests wild living.
items.cn: 该词也暗示放荡的生活。

items.en: Riot comes to mean public disorder.
items.cn: riot 逐渐指公众骚乱。

items.en: Riot police appear to control crowds.
items.cn: 防暴警察出现以控制人群。

items.en: A riot can also mean great fun.
items.cn: a riot 也可以指极大的乐趣。

note.en: A riot is violent; a protest may be peaceful.
note.cn: riot 是暴力的，protest 可能是和平的。

entries.definition: an act that breaks the peace

normalIntro.en: A riot is a crowd that has lost its brakes.
normalIntro.cn: riot 就是失去刹车的人群。

normal.en: Riot police deal with violent crowds.
normal.cn: riot police 应对暴力人群。

normal.en: To start a riot is to cause disorder.
normal.cn: start a riot 就是引发混乱。

normal.en: Run riot means act without control.
normal.cn: run riot 意为失控妄为。

normal.en: A riot of colour means many bright colours.
normal.cn: a riot of colour 意为五彩缤纷。

normal.en: If a show is a riot, it is very funny.
normal.cn: 如果演出是 a riot，就说明它非常逗。

abstract.en: Picture a street full of shouting shadows.
abstract.cn: 想象满是呼喊人影的街道。

abstract.en: Imagine laughter breaking out like a small storm.
abstract.cn: 想象笑声像小风暴一样爆发。

abstract.en: Think of a garden bursting with wild colour.
abstract.cn: 想象花园里色彩狂放。

examples.en: The riot lasted until dawn.
examples.cn: 骚乱持续到黎明。

examples.en: The party was a riot from start to finish.
examples.cn: 这场聚会从头到尾都非常欢乐。

examples.en: The crowd rioted after the decision.
examples.cn: 裁决之后人群发生了暴动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「riot」听起来像「乱特」——特别乱的场面，就是骚乱。

root: 古法语 riote（争吵、放荡）→ 公众骚乱 → 动词「参与暴乱」，核心义「失控的喧嚣」。

sensesIntro.en: A riot is a violent public disturbance, a very funny thing, or the act of rioting.
sensesIntro.cn: riot 指暴力骚乱、极好笑的事物，或参与暴乱的行为。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with no brakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：失去刹车的人群。

branches.en: A violent crowd is the public sense.
branches.cn: 暴力人群是公众义。

branches.en: Uncontrolled laughter borrows the wild image.
branches.cn: 失控的笑借用了狂放的意象。

branches.en: The verb names joining the disorder.

definition_en: ready to eat or ready to happen
core_image: 枝头熟透的桃子
scene: 果园里的桃子已经成熟，等着人来摘。The peaches in the orchard were ripe and ready to pick.

pos.zh: 成熟的；时机成熟的；年高的

senses.definitionCN: 完全长成、可以食用

senses.exampleCN: 这些苹果还没熟。

senses.title: Ready to happen
senses.definition: fully prepared for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为某事的发生做好充分准备
senses.example: The country was ripe for change.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家变革的时机已成熟。
senses.why: A ready time is like fruit ready to fall.
senses.whyCN: 时机成熟就像果实准备落地。

senses.title: Advanced in years
senses.definition: old and full of experience
senses.definitionCN: 年事已高且阅历丰富

items.en: Ripe for change means ready for it.

normal.en: Ripe fruit falls easily from the branch.

normal.en: The time is ripe means now is the moment.

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ripe」听起来像「来盼」——果实盼到最好的时候，就是成熟。

definition_en: the chance that something bad will happen, or to put something in danger

scene: 登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。The climbers set off despite the weather, risking being trapped.
sceneCN: 这里 risk 是「冒…的风险」（第 3 个义项：把某事置于危险之中）；句意：登山者不顾天气变坏，冒着被困山中的风险出发。

senses.title: Chance of harm
senses.definition: the possibility that something bad will happen
senses.definitionCN: 坏事发生的可能性
senses.example: There is a risk of heavy rain tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚有大雨的风险。
senses.why: The noun names the chance of loss before it comes.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指损失尚未发生前的可能性。

senses.title: A dangerous person or thing
senses.definition: someone or something likely to cause harm
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害的人或事物
senses.example: That old bridge is a risk to traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧桥对交通是个隐患。
senses.why: A risk can be the source, not only the chance.
senses.whyCN: 风险也可以指源头，而不只是可能性。

senses.title: To put in danger
senses.definition: to do something that may cause loss or harm

senses.example: He risked his job to help her.

intro.en: Risk comes from French risque, probably from Italian risco, danger.

items.en: Risco means danger or bold chance.

items.en: The verb risk grows beside the noun.

note.en: A risk is a chance of loss; a danger is the harm itself.

normalIntro.en: Risk is the shadow of a bad outcome.
normalIntro.cn: risk 是坏结果的影子。

normal.en: At risk means in danger.

normal.en: Take a risk means accept a chance of loss.

abstract.en: Think of a coin thrown into the dark.

examples.en: They risked everything for the farm.

examples.en: The children are at risk near the river.
examples.cn: 孩子们在河边很危险。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「risk」听起来像「锐思刻」——反复思量那一刻的危险，就是风险。

root: 意大利语 risco（危险）→ 法语 risque → risk，核心义「坏事发生前的可能，以及主动迎向它的行动」。

sensesIntro.en: Risk means the chance of harm, a source of harm, or to put something in danger.
sensesIntro.cn: risk 意为受害的可能、危险的源头，或使某物陷入危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin bridge over a deep drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：深谷上的一座细桥。

branches.en: The chance of loss is the main sense.

branches.en: A dangerous thing is a risk in itself.

branches.en: The verb makes someone face the chance.

branches.en: To risk is to accept the chance of loss.

definition_zh: 按固定程序进行的一套仪式；也指仪式性的
definition_en: a set of actions performed in a fixed order, especially for religious or solemn purposes, and the adjective describing such actions
core_image: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，最年长的人先点上一炷香，其余人依次跟上
scene: 清晨的神龛前摆好米碗与清水，家里最年长的人先点上一炷香。The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
sceneCN: 这里 ritual 指「按固定程序进行的一套仪式」（第 1 个义项：有既定顺序的庄严动作）；句意为节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。可辨识物件：神龛、米碗、清水、香、钟。

senses.title: A set of actions in fixed order
senses.titleCN: 按固定顺序进行的一套动作
senses.definition: a sequence of actions repeated in the same order on the same kind of occasion
senses.definitionCN: 在同类场合按同样顺序重复的一连串动作
senses.example: The opening ritual of the festival begins at dawn with a single bell.
senses.exampleCN: 节日的开场仪式在黎明时以一声钟响开始。
senses.why: ritus named a religious rite, and the noun keeps the idea of an order that must not be varied.
senses.whyCN: ritus 指宗教仪式，这个名词保留了「顺序不可更改」的意思。

senses.title: The ordered rites of worship
senses.definition: the prescribed words and gestures of a religious service
senses.definitionCN: 宗教礼拜中规定的言辞与动作
senses.example: The priest followed the ritual exactly, down to the last bow.
senses.exampleCN: 司仪严格遵循仪式，连最后一次鞠躬也不差。
senses.why: religion is where fixed order is felt to be most necessary, so the word grew strong there.
senses.whyCN: 宗教最能感到固定顺序的必要，这个词也在此处扎根最深。

senses.title: A personal daily routine
senses.definition: a small repeated sequence that marks a part of the day, such as coffee before work
senses.definitionCN: 标记一天中某段时间的重复小序列，如上班前的咖啡
senses.example: Her morning ritual is a cup of tea and ten minutes of silence.
senses.exampleCN: 她的晨间固定程序是一杯茶和十分钟的安静。
senses.why: the word moved from the altar to the kitchen because both need a dependable order.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从祭坛移到厨房，因为两者都需要可靠的顺序。

senses.title: Stylized social courtesy
senses.titleCN: 社会交往中的程式化礼节
senses.definition: the expected words and gestures of greeting, toasting or taking leave
senses.definitionCN: 问候、敬酒或告别时所期待的言辞与动作
senses.example: Their greeting was a ritual of three bows and two questions.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的问候是一套三鞠躬加两个问题的礼节。
senses.why: social life repeats its own small liturgies, and the same noun covers them.
senses.whyCN: 社会生活重复着自己的小礼序，同一个名词也就涵盖了它们。

senses.title: Rites marking a change of status
senses.titleCN: 标记身份转变的过渡仪式
senses.definition: ceremonies such as birth rites, initiation or funerals that move a person from one state to another
senses.definitionCN: 出生礼、成年礼或葬礼等把人从一种状态转入另一种状态的仪式
senses.example: The initiation ritual lasted three days and ended with a new name.
senses.exampleCN: 成年仪式持续三天，最后以一个新名字结束。
senses.why: anthropology found that the most important rituals mark a crossing, not a repetition.
senses.whyCN: 人类学发现最重要的仪式标记的是跨越，而非重复。

senses.title: Repetition that has become compulsive
senses.titleCN: 仪式化的重复行为（心理层面）
senses.definition: a repeated act that calms anxiety or must be performed to avoid distress
senses.definitionCN: 为安抚焦虑而重复、或必须执行以避免痛苦的动作
senses.example: He developed a private ritual of checking the lock four times.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了一个私下的仪式：把锁检查四次。
senses.why: psychology borrowed the word because compulsion has the same outward shape as rite.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借用这个词，因为强迫行为与仪式在外形上相同。

senses.title: Symbolic acts that bind a group
senses.definition: public gestures such as flag-raising or oath-taking that make a group feel itself
senses.definitionCN: 升旗或宣誓等让群体感到自身存在的公开动作
senses.example: The school's Monday ritual assembled every class on the field.
senses.exampleCN: 学校周一的仪式把每个班都召集到操场上。
senses.why: a group needs a body, and repeated gestures give it one.
senses.whyCN: 群体需要一个形体，而重复的动作提供了这个形体。

senses.title: Ritual as an adjective
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of, or used in, a rite'
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前，表示「仪式的」或「仪式中使用的」
senses.example: The ritual dance is performed only by the elders.
senses.exampleCN: 这种仪式之舞只由长者表演。
senses.why: the adjective is simply the noun doing modifying work, a common English shift.
senses.whyCN: 形容词只是名词在起修饰作用，这是英语常见的转用。

senses.title: A fixed routine that feels obligatory
senses.titleCN: 例行公事般的固定做法
senses.definition: a practice repeated so often that it has lost its original purpose
senses.definitionCN: 重复得太频繁、已失去原初目的的做法
senses.example: The weekly meeting had become a ritual nobody questioned.
senses.exampleCN: 每周例会已成了一套无人质疑的例行程序。
senses.why: when order outlives meaning, the word turns slightly ironic.
senses.whyCN: 当顺序比意义活得更久，这个词就带上了一点讽刺。

intro.en: Ritual comes from Latin ritualis 'relating to rites', from ritus 'a rite, a religious ceremony', through Old French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ritual 经古法语来自拉丁 ritualis「与仪式有关的」，而 ritualis 出自 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ritus meant 'a rite, a religious ceremony, a custom'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a Vedic word for fixed order is a hypothesis, not an established derivation.
items.cn: ritus 意为「仪式、宗教典礼、惯例」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与吠陀语中表示「固定秩序」的词相联系，那只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: The suffix -alis made a relational adjective, so ritualis meant 'belonging to a rite' and covered both books and gestures.
items.cn: 后缀 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 ritualis 意为「属于仪式的」，书籍与动作都可用它形容。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective and noun into English, where ritual first named a book of church rites.
items.cn: 古法语把这个形容词与名词带入英语，ritual 最初指记载教会礼仪的书。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the noun meant the rites themselves, and by the nineteenth it had spread to social and personal practice.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，名词已指礼仪本身；到十九世纪，又扩展到社会与个人实践。

items.en: Both disciplines adopted the word, one for rites of passage and the other for compulsive repetition.
items.cn: 人类学与心理学都采用了这个词，前者指过渡仪式，后者指强迫性重复。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of ritus is unsettled, and the earliest use of the ironic 'mere routine' sense is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：ritus 在拉丁语之前的历史尚无定论，讽刺性的「只是例行公事」义的最早用法也只有约略年代。

note.en: Group one holds words built from the same stem; group two holds terms for related solemn or repeated practices.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一词干的词；第二组是表示相关庄严或重复做法的词。

entries.definition: One prescribed ceremony, usually religious or solemn; ritual can name the whole ordered system or the style.
entries.definitionCN: 指单个规定的典礼，通常宗教或庄严；ritual 可指整套有序体系或风格。

entries.definition: Describes something done in the manner of a rite, often with a hint of excess.
entries.definitionCN: 描述以仪式方式完成的事物，常带过度拘泥的暗示。

entries.definition: Excessive attachment to rites, or the study of them as a system.
entries.definitionCN: 指对仪式的过度依附，或把仪式当作体系来研究。

entries.definition: To turn an action into a rite or to perform it in a fixed ceremonial way.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某个动作变成仪式，或以固定礼仪方式完成。

entries.definition: A formal event with a set order; it stresses occasion and dignity more than repeated practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指有固定顺序的正式活动；比「反复实践」更强调场合与庄重。

entries.definition: The prescribed form of public religious worship, usually written down for a congregation.
entries.definitionCN: 指公共宗教礼拜的规定形式，通常为会众写成文本。

entries.definition: The act of keeping a law, feast or custom; it names compliance rather than the sequence of acts.
entries.definitionCN: 指遵守法律、节期或习俗；它指遵从，而非动作序列。

entries.definition: An ordinary repeated way of doing things, without the solemn charge that ritual carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指平常重复的做事方式，不带 ritual 那种庄严意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ritus 'rite' plus -alis 'belonging to' gives 'belonging to a rite'.
normal.cn: ritus「仪式」加 -alis「属于……的」，得到「属于仪式的」。

normal.en: The family runs rite, ritual, ritualistic, ritualism, ritualize and ritualization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 rite、ritual、ritualistic、ritualism、ritualize 与 ritualization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: religious ritual, daily ritual, morning ritual, ritual dance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：宗教仪式、每日固定程序、晨间固定程序、仪式之舞。

normal.en: Anthropology links ritual to rites of passage: a crossing is marked, not merely repeated.
normal.cn: 人类学把仪式与过渡礼仪相连：被标记的是跨越，而不只是重复。

normal.en: The ironic sense appears when a routine outlives its reason, as in a meeting that is a ritual.
normal.cn: 当惯例活得比理由更久，讽刺义就出现，如「一场纯属仪式的会议」。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase whose every step must be taken in the same order.
abstract.cn: 想象一道楼梯，每一级都必须按同样顺序踏过。

abstract.en: Picture a clock that rings not to tell time but to make time feel real.
abstract.cn: 想象一座钟，它响不是为了报时，而是让时间显得真实。

abstract.en: Picture a door that only opens when three hands touch it in turn.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有三只手依次触碰才会打开。

examples.en: The harvest ritual begins with the youngest child pouring water.
examples.cn: 丰收仪式由最小的孩子倒水开始。

examples.en: Modern offices have their own rituals of greeting and leaving.
examples.cn: 现代办公室有自己的问候与告别仪式。

examples.en: The therapist asked whether the ritual reduced his anxiety.
examples.cn: 治疗师问他这套仪式是否减轻了焦虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ri（日）+ tual」——每天按同一顺序做的事，就成了仪式

root: 拉丁 ritus「仪式、宗教典礼」→ ritualis「与仪式有关的」→ 古法语 → 英语 ritual。ritus 的更深来源不确定，与吠陀语「固定秩序」词的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one order: a sequence that must be repeated exactly, performed at an altar, in a kitchen, in a greeting, at a crossing, in a compulsion, on a flagpole and finally in an empty meeting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个顺序展开：一套必须照样重复的动作，依次在祭坛、厨房、问候、人生关口、强迫行为、旗杆前上演，最后落到一场空洞的会议上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of bowls laid out in a fixed order, each filled only when the previous one is full.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排按固定次序摆好的碗，前一只满了才轮到下一只。

branches.en: THE ORDER ITSELF: first a sequence, then the adjective that labels anything belonging to it.
branches.cn: 顺序本身：先是动作序列，再是标记任何属于该序列之物的形容词。

branches.en: ALTAR AND CROSSING: worship repeats the order, while initiation uses it to move a person.
branches.cn: 祭坛与关口：礼拜重复顺序，成年礼则用顺序移动一个人。

branches.en: KITCHEN AND EMPTY MEETING: the same order comforts a morning and hollows out a schedule.
branches.cn: 厨房与空会：同一顺序既安抚一个早晨，也掏空一张日程。

branches.en: COURTESY AND FLAG: small greetings and public gestures both make a group hold together.
branches.cn: 礼节与旗帜：小小问候与公开动作都能让群体维系。

branches.en: COMPULSION: the shape of a rite appears without its meaning, and the repetition becomes a cage.
branches.cn: 强迫：仪式的形状还在，意义却已消失，重复变成牢笼。

intro.en: Ritual is a Latin noun stem with a relational suffix, and that stem also builds the shorter noun rite and the whole ritualistic family.
intro.cn: ritual 是一个拉丁名词词干加关系后缀，同一词干还构成较短的名词 rite 与整个 ritualistic 词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin ritus supplied the stem and -alis supplied the adjective ending; English later added -istic, -ism and -ize to build manner, system and verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ritus 提供词干，-alis 提供形容词词尾；英语后来加上 -istic、-ism 与 -ize，构成方式、体系与动词。

items.example: Ritus named the ceremony before it named the style.
items.exampleCN: ritus 先指典礼，后指风格。

items.example: The suffix makes a relational adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成关系形容词。

items.example: Ritualis covered both the book and the gestures.
items.exampleCN: ritualis 同时涵盖书与动作。

items.example: The noun grew out of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 名词由形容词发展而来。

items.example: Rite is the single act; ritual is the order around it.
items.exampleCN: rite 是单个行为；ritual 是围绕它的顺序。

items.example: Ritualistic means done in the manner of a rite.
items.exampleCN: ritualistic 意为以仪式的方式完成。

items.meaning: in the manner of a rite
items.example: The adjective often hints at excess.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词常暗示过度。

items.example: Ritualize turns an act into a rite.
The room was ritually cleansed before use.
items.exampleCN: 房间在使用前按仪式洁净过。

definition_zh: 对手；竞争者；与…匹敌；竞争的
definition_en: a person or group competing for the same thing, or to match them
core_image: 同一条街上争抢客人的两家小店
scene: 同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。The two shops on the same street are rivals for the same customers.
sceneCN: 这里 rival 是「对手」（第 1 个义项：争夺同一目标的竞争者）；句意：同一条街上的两家店铺互相竞争，争抢同一批客人。

senses.title: One who competes
senses.definition: a person or group trying to win the same thing
senses.definitionCN: 试图赢得同一目标的人或群体
senses.example: Her main rival trains in the same gym.
senses.exampleCN: 她的主要对手在同一家健身房训练。
senses.why: Two people sharing one stream must compete for it.
senses.whyCN: 共用一条溪流的人必然要争夺它。

senses.title: To match someone
senses.definition: to be as good as someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 与某人或某物一样出色
senses.example: No one can rival her skill at chess.
senses.exampleCN: 没人能在棋艺上与她匹敌。
senses.why: A worthy opponent raises the level of both.
senses.whyCN: 强劲的对手会把双方的水平都抬高。

senses.title: Competing
senses.definition: competing for the same market or aim
senses.definitionCN: 争夺同一市场或目标的
senses.example: The rival firm cut its prices.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手公司降低了价格。
senses.why: The adjective marks the other side of the race.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标记竞赛的另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivalis, one who uses the same stream, from rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 源自拉丁语 rivalis，意为共用同一条溪流的人，来自 rivus（溪流）。

items.en: Rivus means a stream.
items.cn: rivus 意为溪流。

items.en: Rivalis is one who shares the stream.
items.cn: rivalis 指共用溪流的人。

items.en: French rival keeps the sense of a competitor.
items.cn: 法语 rival 保留了竞争者的含义。

items.en: English rival names a rival in love or sport.
items.cn: 英语 rival 指情感或竞技中的对手。

items.en: Business gives the word its widest use.
items.cn: 商业让这个词使用最广。

note.en: A rival is close enough to compete; an enemy wishes to harm.
note.cn: rival 是实力相当、彼此竞争的对手，enemy 是想伤害对方的人。

entries.definition: the other side in a contest

normalIntro.en: Rivals once shared one stream and fought over it.
normalIntro.cn: rival 原本指共用一条溪流并为之争夺的人。

normal.en: A rival company wants your customers.
normal.cn: rival company 想要你的顾客。

normal.en: A business rival is a firm you compete with.
normal.cn: business rival 是与你在生意上竞争的公司。

normal.en: A rival team stands on the other side.
normal.cn: rival team 站在赛场的另一边。

normal.en: An arch rival is your biggest opponent.
normal.cn: arch rival 是你最大的对手。

normal.en: Rivalry is the noun for the fight between them.
normal.cn: rivalry 是双方对抗的名词。

abstract.en: Picture two farmers at one narrow ditch.
abstract.cn: 想象两个农夫在一条窄渠两端。

abstract.en: Imagine two runners shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象两名跑者肩并着肩。

abstract.en: Think of two shop signs facing each other.
abstract.cn: 想象两块店招面对面挂起。

examples.en: The two cities are rivals for the trade.
examples.cn: 这两座城市是贸易上的竞争对手。

examples.en: Nobody could rival his patience.
examples.cn: 没有人能比得上他的耐心。

examples.en: A rival seller opened next door.
examples.cn: 一位竞争卖家在隔壁开了店。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rival」听起来像「来否」——总来争抢同一个目标的，就是对手。

root: 拉丁语 rivus（溪流）→ rivalis（共用溪流者）→ rival，核心义「争夺同一资源、实力相当的对手」。

sensesIntro.en: A rival competes for the same goal, can match another's ability, or acts as a competing force.
sensesIntro.cn: rival 指争夺同一目标的对手，也可指与某人匹敌，或作形容词表示竞争的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at one narrow stream.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人在一条窄溪旁。

branches.en: The competitor is the main noun sense.
branches.cn: 竞争者是最主要的名词义项。

branches.en: To match a rival is to reach their level.
branches.cn: 与对手匹敌就是达到他们的水平。

branches.en: The adjective marks the opposite side.
branches.cn: 形容词标记对立的一方。

branches.en: Real rivals make each other stronger.
branches.cn: 真正的对手让彼此更强。

branches.en: The noun and adjective both name the other side.
branches.cn: 名词与形容词都指另一方。

intro.en: Rival comes from Latin rivus, a stream.
intro.cn: rival 来自拉丁语 rivus（溪流）。

latinIntro.en: Rivalis, one who shares a stream, gives the French and English word.
latinIntro.cn: rivalis（共用溪流的人）给出了法语和英语中的这个词。

latinEntries.example: Rivus explains why rivals share water.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivus 解释了对手为何共享水源。

latinEntries.example: Rivalis is the source of rival.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rivalis 是 rival 的来源。

definition_en: to cook with dry heat, roasted meat, or to tease someone publicly
core_image: 烤箱里慢慢转动的整只鸡
scene: 厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。In the kitchen, father put the whole chicken in the oven to roast slowly.
sceneCN: 这里 roast 是「烤」（第 1 个义项：用干热烹制食物）；句意：厨房里，父亲把整只鸡放进烤箱，让它慢慢烤。

senses.title: Cooking with dry heat
senses.definition: to cook food with dry heat in an oven or over fire
senses.definitionCN: 在烤箱中或用火以干热烹调食物
senses.example: Roast the nuts for ten minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 把坚果烤十分钟。
senses.why: Dry heat browns and deepens the food.
senses.whyCN: 干热让食物上色并加深风味。

senses.title: Roasted meat
senses.definition: a piece of meat cooked in dry heat
senses.definitionCN: 用干热烹制的一块肉
senses.example: The Sunday roast was wonderful.
senses.exampleCN: 周日的烤肉大餐棒极了。
senses.why: The noun names what the oven has made.
senses.whyCN: 名词指烤箱做出来的东西。

senses.title: Teasing in public
senses.definition: to criticize or joke about someone in a friendly or comic way
senses.definitionCN: 以友好或滑稽的方式公开批评、打趣某人
senses.example: The show roasted a famous actor.
senses.exampleCN: 这档节目公开调侃了一位著名演员。
senses.why: Comedy heat teases without burning.
senses.whyCN: 喜剧的火候，调侃而不灼伤。

intro.en: Roast comes from Old French rostir, to roast.
intro.cn: roast 源自古法语 rostir，意为烤。

items.en: Rostir means to roast over fire.
items.cn: rostir 意为在火上烤。

items.en: Roast enters English as a cooking verb.
items.cn: roast 以烹饪动词之意进入英语。

items.en: The noun names a joint of meat.
items.cn: 名词指一大块烤肉。

items.en: Roast extends to coffee and nuts.
items.cn: roast 扩展到咖啡与坚果。

items.en: The comic roast gives a joking sense.
items.cn: 喜剧调侃节目赋予它开玩笑的义项。

note.en: Roast uses dry heat; boil uses water.
note.cn: roast 用干热，boil 用水。

entries.definition: a pan or machine for roasting
to cook under or over strong heat

normalIntro.en: To roast is to let dry heat do the work.
normalIntro.cn: roast 就是让干热来完成工作。

normal.en: Roast beef is a classic Sunday dish.
normal.cn: roast beef 是经典的周日菜肴。

normal.en: Roast chicken fills the kitchen with smell.
normal.cn: roast chicken 让厨房充满香味。

normal.en: Roast potatoes turn golden in the oven.
normal.cn: roast potatoes 在烤箱里变成金黄。

normal.en: A Sunday roast brings the family together.
normal.cn: a Sunday roast 让一家人聚在一起。

normal.en: To roast a friend is to tease them kindly.
normal.cn: roast 朋友就是善意地打趣。

abstract.en: Picture a chicken turning slowly above coals.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸡在炭火上慢慢转动。

abstract.en: Imagine the kitchen warm and full of steam.
abstract.cn: 想象厨房温暖、蒸汽弥漫。

abstract.en: Think of a comedian's gentle fire on stage.
abstract.cn: 想象喜剧演员在台上燃起的温和之火。

examples.en: We roasted vegetables for dinner.
examples.cn: 我们烤了蔬菜当晚餐。

examples.en: He ordered the roast with potatoes.
examples.cn: 他点了烤肉配土豆。

examples.en: The comic roasted the whole team.
examples.cn: 这位喜剧演员把整支队伍都调侃了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「roast」听起来像「热死它」——用热力把它烘透，就是烤。

root: 古法语 rostir（在火上烤）→ roast，核心义「用干热使食物变熟上色」，再引申出公开「烤」人的调侃义。

sensesIntro.en: Roast means to cook with dry heat, the meat so cooked, or to tease someone publicly.
sensesIntro.cn: roast 意为用干热烹调、这样烤出的肉，或公开调侃某人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dry heat browning food.
core.cn: 核心意象：干热让食物上色。

branches.en: Cooking with dry heat is the core sense.
branches.cn: 干热烹制是核心义项。

branches.en: The noun names the finished meat.
branches.cn: 名词指烤好的肉。

branches.en: Comic teasing borrows the heat image.
branches.cn: 喜剧调侃借用了热度意象。

branches.en: The verb and its product share one word.
branches.cn: 动作与其产物共用一个词。

branches.en: Both real fire and comic fire need good control.
branches.cn: 真实的火与喜剧的火都需要掌控火候。

intro.en: Roast is a French borrowing from rostir.
intro.cn: roast 是来自 rostir 的法语借词。

latinIntro.en: The French verb is its direct parent.
latinIntro.cn: 法语动词是它的直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指一种传统。

definition_zh: 机器人；自动机械；呆板的人
definition_en: a machine that performs tasks by itself, or any self-running device, or a person who acts without feeling
core_image: 流水线上一只机械臂举起零件，关节转动时发出轻响
scene: 流水线上一只机械臂举起零件，关节转动时发出轻响。The robot arm lifted the heavy box.
sceneCN: 这里 robot 是「机器人」（第 01 个义项）；句意是机械臂抬起了沉重的箱子。

pos.zh: 名词：机器人、自动机械、呆板的人

senses.title: A machine that performs tasks by itself
senses.definition: A machine that performs tasks by itself
senses.definitionCN: 能自行完成任务的机器
senses.example: The robot arm lifted the heavy box.
senses.exampleCN: 机械臂抬起了沉重的箱子。
senses.why: Robot came from Czech robota, forced labour, and was coined for a machine that works like a servant.
senses.whyCN: robot 源自捷克语 robota（苦役），被造出来指像仆役一样干活的机器。

senses.title: Any machine that works on its own
senses.definition: Any machine that works on its own
senses.definitionCN: 自行运转的装置
senses.example: The vacuum robot cleans the floor each night.
senses.exampleCN: 扫地机器人每晚清理地板。
senses.why: Because the first robots were automatic workers, the name spread to any self-running machine in a home.
senses.whyCN: 因为最早的机器人就是自动干活的，这个名字就扩展到家中自行运转的机器。

senses.title: A person who acts like a machine
senses.definition: A person who acts like a machine
senses.definitionCN: 像机器一样行事的人
senses.example: He answers like a robot, without feeling.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答得像机器人，毫无感情。
senses.why: When a person seems to work without feeling, the word is used as an image of the machine.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人做事像没有感情，这个词就被拿来比喻那台机器。

intro.en: The history of robot is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: robot 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.en: Robota meant forced labour.
items.cn: 捷克语 robota 意为苦役。

items.en: A play used it for a machine.
items.cn: 一部戏剧用它来称机器。

items.en: Machines took over tasks.
items.cn: 机器替人干活。

items.en: A dull person is called a robot.
items.cn: 呆板的人被叫作机器人。

items.en: Robot covers machines and manner.
items.cn: 现代英语中它涵盖机器与人的做派。

note.cn: 形近组收拼写、词根或构词相近的词；近义组收同一日常语义场里的词。

abstract.cn: 想象流水线上一只机械臂举起零件，关节转动时发出轻响，再让画面变大变小，直到它同时罩住日常实物与比喻用法。

abstract.en: Place the word inside the scene given in this entry; what stays in memory is the picture, not the translation.
abstract.cn: 把 robot 放进本词条给出的场景里；留在记忆里的是画面，不是翻译。

abstract.en: Link the word to one object you can point at, then to the idea that object lends to the other senses.
abstract.cn: 把 robot 与一件能指认的具体事物挂钩，再挂到该事物借给其他义项的那层意思。

examples.en: The robot arm lifted the heavy box.
examples.cn: 机械臂抬起了沉重的箱子。

examples.en: The vacuum robot cleans the floor each night.
examples.cn: 扫地机器人每晚清理地板。

examples.en: He answers like a robot, without feeling.
examples.cn: 他回答得像机器人，毫无感情。

sensesIntro.en: Robot means a machine that performs tasks by itself, and it also means any self-running device, or a person who acts without feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: robot 指能自行完成任务的机器，也指任何自行运转的装置，或像机器一样没有感情的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a robot arm lifting a part on an assembly line, its joints turning with a soft whir
core.cn: 核心意象：流水线上一只机械臂举起零件，关节转动时发出轻响

branches.en: MACHINE: lifting a box.
branches.cn: 机器线：抬起重箱。

branches.en: DEVICE: a vacuum at night.
branches.cn: 装置线：夜里的扫地机。

branches.en: PERSON: answering coldly.
branches.cn: 人物线：冷淡作答。

branches.en: LINE: joints whirring.
branches.cn: 流水线：关节作响。

branches.en: PLAY: the name from a play.
branches.cn: 戏剧线：剧中的名称。

intro.cn: 这个词可以拆成主词与它所用的普通英语词尾。

latinIntro.cn: 凡有文献可查的拉丁来源，相关形式列在下面。

items.meaningCN: 本词条使用的主词形式
items.example: The headword carries the senses listed in this entry.
items.exampleCN: 这一主词承载了本词条列出的各个义项。

items.meaningCN: 同一主词的语法变化形式
items.example: robots belongs to the same headword.

items.exampleCN: 英语在大量单词与词族中使用这一构词模式。

items.meaningCN: 表示过去式或过去分词
items.example: English uses this pattern across many words and word families.
